title: Phasegate KPI Thermostat & Exit Controls
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a compact working sheet used by Product Ops to drive phase-gate decisions for feature launches. It combines a live KPI "thermostat" (observe, decide, act), explicit exit/abort criteria, and a short contingency playbook for each failure mode. Use this during the final 14-day runway and for canary-to-scale transitions.

How to use this file (quick):
- Owner updates the KPI row daily during final 7 days, every other day prior.
- Each KPI has a target band (green/yellow/red). Any red triggers a triage call.
- If >2 independent reds persist for 24h, run the abort checklist and escalate to GTM lead.

KPI thermostat (live inputs expected):
- Latency (p50/p95): target p50 < 180ms, p95 < 420ms. Acceptance: green if both met; yellow if p95 between 420-650ms; red if p95 > 650ms. Owner: infra-SRE (Miguel Torres).
- Error rate (api 5xx+client-side failures): target <0.5% 24h rolling. Yellow 0.5-1.5%, red >1.5%. Owner: platform eng (Evan Brooks).
- Cost per 1k requests (token-normalized): target <$0.60. Yellow $0.60-0.95, red >$0.95. Owner: product-ops finance liaison (Priya Nair).
- Quality regression (eval score A/B vs baseline on canonical prompt set): target delta >= -1.5%. Yellow -1.5% to -3.0%, red < -3.0%. Owner: applied-ml (Asha Patel).
- Adoption velocity (first-week DAU conversion for beta cohort): target >12% conversion. Yellow 8-12%, red <8%. Owner: growth/gfm.
- Support volume (tickets/day attributable to change): target <5/day. Yellow 5-12/day, red >12/day. Owner: customer-success.

Exit (go/no-go) decision matrix (final review window):
- Green across key SLOs (Latency, Error rate, Quality): proceed to scale.
- Any single red but compensating blameless mitigation and a one-week rollout hold with targeted fixes: may proceed to phased rollout only with explicit mitigation plan.
- Two or more reds concurrently, or single critical regression in Quality (red): abort rollout and revert to last stable variant.
- Regulatory or security blockers discovered at any time: immediate stop and incident response.

Abort checklist (short):
1) Notify stakeholders: product, eng, SRE, CS, legal. Use Slack channel + email.
2) Run fallback: switch traffic to pinned stable model/route; cut feature gate flag.
3) Open post-mortem ticket: JIRA template link in linked_artifacts. Owner: release lead.
4) Preserve telemetry: snapshot traces, logs, and evaluation prompts.
5) Customer outreach: CS owns 24h notice cadence for impacted beta orgs.

Contingency playbook (by failure mode):
- High latency: reduce batch size, increase instance count for latency tier, enable KV caching for stable prefixes. Short-term mitigation owner: infra. Medium-term: model quantization profile.
- Elevated cost: throttle non-critical routes, enable per-route cost caps, switch to lower-cost model variant for bulk traffic. Owner: product-ops + finance.
- Quality regression: initiate targeted rollback of model checkpoint, run prompt-level rollback for failing cohorts, escalate eval owner for urgent fixes. Owner: applied-ml.
- Spike in support tickets: deploy targeted KB article, increase CS triage headcount, enable temporary in-app help messaging. Owner: customer-success.

Open questions & unresolved risks:
- Can we guarantee parity for private deployments where runtime kernels differ? (action: infra to confirm measurable variance by 2024-10-01)
- Are we comfortable with cost-surge thresholds for free-tier customers? (finance to propose hard caps)
- Beta cohort size dependency: current sample n=48 — not statistically robust for rare fault modes. Recommendation: enlarge cohort and run synthetic load.

Acceptance artifacts required before scale (tick when present):
- Final SLO report for 72h rolling window (artifact link).
- Runbook tested in chaos window (screenshot of runbook run).
- Customer communication draft approved by CS and legal.
- Post-canary evaluation (A/B eval) with p-value and uplift estimate.

Owner matrix (single-line):
- Release lead: Priya Nair; Product TL: Asha Patel; Infra/SRE: Miguel Torres; Applied ML: Asha Patel; Platform: Evan Brooks; CS lead: Jamie Liu.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the thermostat narrow: do not overload with vanity metrics. Focus on latency, error, cost, quality, and support.
- When in doubt, prefer rollback + fix vs slow degradation.

Audit trail expectations:
- Every decision must have a short comment in this sheet with timestamp and link to the JIRA or Slack thread.

References and templates:
- See linked_artifacts for immediate links. Use JIRA template PROD-ROLLBACK-TEMPLATE when creating post-mortem.

Recent changes (journal):
- 2024-09-12: tightened cost band after infra reforecast.
- 2024-08-01: added support-volume metric and playbook.

End of sheet. Keep compact, update early and often during launch runway.
